newsitem.title: USA: Florida Power extends Crystal River outage.
newsitem.headline: Florida Power extends Crystal River outage.

text.p: Florida Power Corp said Tuesday it is extending an outage at its Crystal River nuclear power plant, possibly until the fourth quarter, and seeking a rate increase to help cover fuel costs linked to the outage.
The 860 megawatt (MW) unit, shut in September, 1996, is undergoing an extensive upgrade, including resolving several design issues.
One issue is linked to electrical loading on one of the plant's two emergency diesel generators, which would provide power to the emergency core cooling system in the event of a power failure.

"Company management is reviewing possible options to resolve the loading issue. Under any of the alternatives, the company's nuclear engineers have determined that resolving the generator issue will extend the outage beyond the original restart date of February 28," FPC said in a statement.
The company said that if preliminary tests, scheduled to end in April, show the upgrades are successful, the plant could restart in the fourth quarter of 1997.
FPC said the extended outage has prompted it to seek an increase in the fuel expense portion of the bills it sends customers.

"The average 1,000-kilowatt-hour bill for residential customers would increase from $83.39 to $88.65, effective April 1. This increase is subject to approval by the Florida Public Service Commission," it said.
The additional charge represents the cost of replacement power during the outage and higher oil and natural gas prices.
The commission meets twice a year to consider rate adjustments for the state's investor-owned utilities. Its next meeting is set for February 19-21.

"We are working diligently to return the nuclear plant to service. The impact to bills is higher than we would like. However, we believe the steps we are taking will reduce costs to our customers in the long term by ensuring the plant resumes its strong performance record," said Joe Richardson, president and chief operating officer of Florida Power Corp.
"We are very sensitive...to increases for our customers. To lessen the impact, we are asking that these fuel costs be spread out over a 12-month period instead of the customary six," Richardson said.
FPC, Florida's second-biggest electric utility, is the principal subsidiary of St. Petersburg-based Florida Progress Corp and serves 1.3 million customers in central and northern Florida.
The Crystal River nuclear facility is in Red Level, Fla.
